paper.title_en: Systematic comparison of driving potentials: Benchmarking and prediction for <math><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi>Ca</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>48</mn></mmultiscripts><mo>+</mo><mmultiscripts><mi>Es</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>254</mn></mmultiscripts></mrow></math>
paper.abstract_en: The synthesis of the superheavy element with atomic number <math><mrow><mi>Z</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>119</mn></mrow></math> via the <math><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi>Ca</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>48</mn></mmultiscripts><mo>+</mo><mmultiscripts><mi>Es</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>254</mn></mmultiscripts></mrow></math> reaction represents one of the most promising near-term experimental goals, although theoretical predictions of its evaporation residue cross section (ERCS) are consistently low. Within the dinuclear system (DNS) model, the driving potential <math><mrow><mi>U</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>η</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> provides the microscopic landscape governing nucleon transfer and compound-nucleus formation. We therefore examine how different microscopic inputs modify the fusion path and ERCS predictions for <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Ca</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>48</mn></mmultiscripts></math>-induced reactions on <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Cm</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>248</mn></mmultiscripts><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mmultiscripts><mi>Cf</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>249</mn></mmultiscripts></math>, and <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Es</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>254</mn></mmultiscripts></math>. Calculations based on finite-range droplet model (FRDM) and Weizsäcker-Skyrme (WS) microscopic-macroscopic models are compared, with the former two benchmark reactions evaluated against available experimental data. Within the WS model, explicitly introducing deformation parameters <math><mrow><mo>(</mo><msub><mi>β</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>β</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> as independent degrees of freedom reduces the Coulomb potential at the entrance channel, thereby lowering the inner fusion barrier by approximately 1 MeV. The inclusion of shell-correction damping at finite excitation energy further modifies the driving potential and fusion probability <math><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>CN</mi></msub></math> within the optimized deformation scheme. For the <math><mrow><mn>3</mn><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> evaporation channel of <math><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi>Ca</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>48</mn></mmultiscripts><mo>+</mo><mmultiscripts><mi>Es</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>254</mn></mmultiscripts></mrow></math>, predicted ERCS lies in the range of [0.016,0.167] pb around the favorable excitation-energy region of <math><mrow><msup><mi>E</mi><mo>*</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>32</mn><mo>–</mo><mn>34</mn></mrow></math> MeV. The comparison with previous theoretical studies indicates that the energy region is relatively robust, whereas the absolute cross section exhibits substantial model dependence. These results provide a quantitative assessment of microscopic uncertainties in driving potential calculations for future <math><mrow><mi>Z</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>119</mn></mrow></math> synthesis studies.
